chapters.title: Return to God and receive comfort

parts.text: Zechariah calls the people to return to the LORD, who promises to return to them. They must not repeat their fathers’ refusal to hear the prophets. Though both fathers and prophets have died, God’s words overtook the earlier generation, who acknowledged that he had dealt with them according to their conduct.

In a night vision, riders report that the earth is at rest, and an angel asks how long Jerusalem must remain afflicted. God answers with comfort and promises to rebuild his house and prosper his cities. Zechariah then sees four horns representing powers that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, followed by four carpenters sent to overthrow those powers.

Zechariah sees a man preparing to measure Jerusalem. An angel announces that the city will overflow ordinary walls because of its many people and animals. The LORD himself will be a wall of fire around it and its glory within. Its security will rest in his presence.

The scattered people are called to flee the northern land and escape Babylon. God will act against nations that plundered them, treating injury to his people as injury to the apple of his eye. Zion is urged to rejoice because he will dwell among it. Many nations will join themselves to the LORD, Judah will be his portion, and all flesh is called to silence before him.

chapters.title: Joshua cleansed and the Branch promised

parts.text: Joshua the high priest stands before the angel of the LORD in filthy garments, with Satan opposing him. The LORD rebukes Satan and describes Joshua as a brand rescued from fire. His dirty garments are removed as a sign that his iniquity has passed away, and he receives clean clothing and a fair miter.

Joshua is charged to walk in God’s ways and keep his service, with promised responsibility in the house and courts. He and his companions are signs connected with God’s coming servant, the Branch. A stone with seven eyes is set before Joshua, and God promises to remove the land’s iniquity in one day. Neighbors will then sit together beneath vine and fig tree.

chapters.title: The candlestick and the Spirit’s power

parts.text: Zechariah sees a candlestick all of gold with seven lamps and two olive trees. The accompanying message tells Zerubbabel that the work will be accomplished by God’s Spirit rather than human might. Obstacles pictured as a great mountain will become level, and the man who laid the temple’s foundation will also finish it. The day of small things must not be despised.

Zechariah asks specifically about the olive trees and branches supplying golden oil through pipes. The angel identifies them as two anointed ones standing beside the Lord of the whole earth. The vision combines the assurance of God’s sustaining provision with the promise that the temple work entrusted to Zerubbabel will reach completion.

chapters.title: The flying scroll and the woman in the ephah

parts.text: Zechariah sees a flying scroll twenty cubits long and ten wide. It represents a curse going over the earth against theft and false swearing. The LORD will send it into the offender’s house, where it will remain and consume the building, timber and stones together. Hidden wrongdoing will not escape its reach.

A second vision shows a woman enclosed in an ephah beneath a lead cover. The angel explicitly identifies her as wickedness and confines her within the vessel. Two winged women lift it between earth and heaven. Zechariah is told that they carry it to Shinar, where a house will be prepared and the ephah established in its place.

Four chariots emerge between mountains of brass, drawn by differently colored horses. The angel identifies them as the four spirits of heaven going out from the Lord’s presence. They travel through the earth, and those sent north are said to have quieted God’s spirit in that country.

Zechariah must receive silver and gold from returned captives, make crowns, and place them on Joshua the high priest. He announces the man called the Branch, who will build the LORD’s temple and rule as a priest upon his throne. The crowns remain as a memorial. People from far away will help build, and the closing promise is expressly linked to diligent obedience to the LORD.

Representatives ask whether mourning in the fifth month should continue as in previous years. The LORD answers by questioning whether their fasting and feasting were truly directed toward him. The issue is the same word spoken by earlier prophets when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were prosperous.

God required honest judgment, mercy, compassion, and protection for widows, orphans, strangers, and the poor. He forbade inward schemes against neighbors. The fathers refused to listen, hardened their hearts, and rejected the law and prophetic words sent by his Spirit. Therefore their cries went unanswered, they were scattered among unfamiliar nations, and the pleasant land became desolate.

chapters.title: Restoration, truthful living, and joyful feasts

parts.text: The LORD declares his return to Zion and promises that Jerusalem will be known for truth and holiness. Its streets will again hold the elderly and playing children. He will gather his people from east and west, renew their relationship with him, and replace former insecurity with fruitful harvests. Those rebuilding the temple are urged to take courage.

God calls the people to speak truth, judge faithfully, reject harmful schemes, and refuse false oaths. Their fasts will become joyful festivals, so they should love truth and peace. Peoples and strong nations will seek the LORD in Jerusalem. Men from many languages will take hold of a Jew’s garment, asking to accompany him because they have heard that God is with his people.

chapters.title: Zion’s humble king and promised rescue

parts.text: Judgment is announced on neighboring territories, including Tyrus, whose wealth and sea power cannot protect it. Philistine cities lose their pride and security, though a remnant is brought into relation with God. The Lord promises to guard his house against passing armies and oppressive invaders.

Zion is called to rejoice because its righteous king comes humbly riding an ass. He brings peace to the nations and dominion to the earth’s ends. By the blood of the covenant, prisoners are released and invited to return as prisoners of hope. God defends his people, using Judah and Ephraim against Greece, and saves them like a cherished flock and the precious stones of a crown.

chapters.title: The scattered flock strengthened and gathered

parts.text: The people should ask the LORD for rain rather than trust idols and diviners, whose promises are false. Israel has wandered like a flock without a shepherd. God confronts the failed shepherds, visits Judah, and strengthens his people for battle. He promises mercy to Judah and Joseph, restoring them as though they had not been rejected.

Ephraim and its children will rejoice in the LORD. He will summon and gather the redeemed, who remember him even in distant countries. Their return from Egypt and Assyria will fill Gilead and Lebanon. Obstacles pictured as sea and river will be overcome, foreign pride will fall, and the people will live in the strength of the LORD’s name.

chapters.title: The rejected shepherd and broken staffs

parts.text: A lament announces the fall of proud forests and the distress of shepherds. Zechariah is told to shepherd a flock destined for slaughter, whose owners exploit it without pity. He takes two staffs, Beauty and Bands, but encounters rejection. Breaking Beauty signifies the breaking of a covenant, and the attentive poor recognize the LORD’s word.

The shepherd’s assessed payment is thirty pieces of silver, which God commands to be cast to the potter in the LORD’s house. Breaking Bands signifies the broken brotherhood of Judah and Israel. Zechariah then portrays a foolish shepherd who neglects the vulnerable and consumes the flock. A woe announces judgment upon the arm and eye of the shepherd who abandons his charge.

The Creator declares that Jerusalem will become a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone to attacking nations. Their forces will be confused, while Judah’s leaders become like fire among dry wood. God will save Judah and defend Jerusalem, strengthening even the weak and seeking the destruction of the nations that come against it.

The LORD will pour out a spirit of grace and supplication upon David’s house and Jerusalem. They will look upon the one they pierced and mourn bitterly, as for an only son or firstborn. The grief extends through the land, with named families and all remaining households mourning separately, including husbands and wives. Public deliverance is thus joined with personal and communal lamentation.

A fountain is opened for the sin and uncleanness of David’s house and Jerusalem. God removes idols, false prophecy, and the unclean spirit from the land. Those claiming false messages face rejection even within their families. Prophets become ashamed of their visions and stop using deceptive outward signs. A man denies being a prophet, calling himself an husbandman. Asked, ‘What are these wounds in thine hands?’ he answers, ‘Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.’

The LORD summons a sword against his shepherd, and the sheep scatter. Two parts in the land are cut off, while a third remains. God brings this remnant through refining fire like silver and gold. They call on his name and receive his answer: he acknowledges them as his people, and they acknowledge him as their God.

chapters.title: The Lord comes to reign over the earth

parts.text: Nations gather against Jerusalem, capturing the city and carrying half its people away. The LORD then fights those nations, and his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits to form a valley of escape. He comes with his saints. A unique day, living waters from Jerusalem, transformed land, and secure habitation accompany his kingship over all the earth.

The attacking peoples suffer plague and confusion, and their wealth is gathered. Survivors from the nations must come yearly to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles; refusal brings withheld rain and judgment. Holiness extends beyond temple vessels to ordinary pots and even horses’ bells. The LORD’s house is no longer occupied by a Canaanite.
